sections.overview: Hispidoberyx ambagiosus is a rarely collected deep-sea fish and the sole described species in the family Hispidoberycidae.
sections.identification: It has a slender, laterally compressed body with conspicuous spiny scales; its detailed morphology has been redescribed from Taiwanese specimens.
sections.habitat: Available records place it in deep marine waters from the eastern Indian Ocean and South China Sea to northeastern Taiwan, at about 560–1,019 m depth.
sections.diet: FishBase reports shrimp in its diet, but this account is based on very few specimens and does not establish a detailed feeding ecology.
sections.behavior: Its behavior is poorly known; the species is described as probably benthopelagic rather than as a fish with a well-documented daily routine.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted do not provide a species-level account of courtship, spawning or parental care.
sections.ecology: Current accounts treat its family as monotypic, with no described congener for direct comparison. The Taiwanese redescription extends the species’ known northern limit.
sections.conservation: FishBase reproduces a Least Concern assessment dated 22 December 2019, but the rarity of collected specimens leaves important aspects of its biology uncertain.
